name: scripts
title: Scripts and data files
description: Lists from shell scripts and data files, with no extension to write: point it at a script that prints JSON lines, a JSON or TOML file, or a folder of script commands. Raycast script commands work as they are.
author: pal

settings.label: v1 config
settings.description: A pal v1 config.toml; every [palette.<name>] in it becomes a palette here.

settings.label: Skip
settings.description: v1 palette names not to load, because a native extension covers them.

settings.label: v1 checkout
settings.description: The v1 checkout: where github:zcag/pal/... bases resolve when v1's plugin cache (~/.local/share/pal) has no copy, and where a base under a v1 checkout missing on this box is looked up. ~/proj/pal is tried when this path has no plugins.

settings.label: Script commands
settings.description: A folder of single-file script commands: every executable in it with a # @pal.title line in its header (or Raycast's # @raycast.title) is one row of the Script Commands palette. Watched: a saved file shows on the next listing.

settings.label: Script timeout
settings.description: A list or pick script still running after this is killed.

settings.label: Previews at once
settings.description: An item's preview command runs when the detail pane rests on it; at most this many run at the same time. 0 turns previews off.

settings.label: Listing lifetime
settings.description: A palette that declares no ttl keeps its last listing across restarts and shows for this long before its script runs again; a palette's own ttl wins, and a live palette is exempt (it relists on every show unless it sets its own). Default an hour: scripts are the slow tier, and the root answers from the kept listing meanwhile. 0 runs every script on every start.

store.tagline: Lists from shell scripts, data files and script commands
features: Each `[palette.<name>]` in your config becomes its own list in the panel
A data file (JSON, JSON lines or TOML) becomes rows with titles, subtitles, links and sections
A script answers with JSON lines and can copy, open, show a message or drill into another list
Script commands: one row per executable in a folder with a `# @pal.title` header, arguments typed in the bar
Lists that refresh on every keystroke or every open, and a detail pane from a shell command

screenshots.caption: A data-file palette: the rows of links.json in sections, the table's icon unless a row brings its own
A script palette: the rows run.sh printed as JSON lines, with sections and tags
A script palette's rows are searchable from the root: deploy finds both deploy commands and the deploy script
Script Commands: one row per script in the folder, its mode on the right, an inline one's latest output as its subtitle
A list-mode command: the lines its script printed become rows of their own
A command with @pal.args asks for them before it runs: here the deploy's target and a note

actions.title: Open
actions.description: An `open` action on the row's url.

actions.title: Copy link
actions.description: A `copy` action on a row field.

actions.title: Select
actions.description: The default of a script palette without actions: run.sh pick with the row in the environment.

actions.title: Run
actions.description: A script command, as its mode says: hud shows the first output line, show the whole output, list its rows, silent nothing. Its @pal.args are typed in the bar first ($1, $2, ... in header order). Asks first with @pal.confirm.

actions.title: Open script
actions.description: The command's file in its editor.

actions.title: Copy output
actions.description: Runs the command and copies what it printed; its @pal.args are typed in the bar first.
